messages:
incident-bot: Pager: p99 latency breach for hosted-streaming-eu (model=redwood-small-8q). p99=3.2s > SLO(1.5s). Start=2065432199. Suspected infra. Severity: P2. Link: https://infrig/redwood/incident/2065432199

sanjay: seeing same in prod dashboards — p95 ~800ms (baseline ~120ms). streaming sessions showing stalls/partial payloads. any gpu errors in node logs?

katie: pulled node logs from eu-west1/gpu-node-42. lots of ECC correctable messages + thermal trips. snippets below:
```
[ 1234.567890] GPU0: ECC error corrected: 0x1a
[ 1234.567891] thermal: GPU0: temperature above threshold, throttling active
[ 1234.568001] nvidia-smi: GPU 0 Throttle: Thermal
```

maria: @sanjay can we confirm autoscale didn't just put more load on that node? also any in-flight streaming count?

sanjay: autoscaler showing even distribution, but this node had higher slot density due to sticky routing. in-flight sessions: 4 long-lived streams pinned -> likely KV cache hot -> cold after drain.

james: starting evacuation of gpu-node-42 now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m` — moving pods to dedicated-pool-eu and cpu-fallback pool.

opsbot: Evacuation job started for gpu-node-42. Migrated 12 inference pods so far, 6 remaining. 4 streaming sessions flagged for graceful migration.

elaine: temporarily enabling route fallback: stream sessions >25s -> cpu-infer-eu, and short-circuit streaming to quantized variant to avoid stalls. will monitor p95/p99. :rocket:

sanjay: after partial drain p99 dropped to ~1.0s but p95 still elevated ~350ms. suspected KV cache cold-starts causing higher p95. rehydrating prefix cache for high-throughput customers.

maria: CS note: logged brief 502s for some customers between 2065432205-2065432218; creating customer-impact ticket and flagging top customers in EU. No data exposure.

katie: hardware team says fan on gpu-node-42 is spiking RPM then dropping, temps hitting 95C and causing repeated thermal throttles. Opening a hardware replacement ticket (DC-2026-987). Recommend cordon node until replacement.

elaine: I'll hand off the remainder to night oncall. @james you take primary? I'll leave runbook notes and the mitigation config.

james: taking over. Will cordon gpu-node-42 (`kubectl cordon gpu-node-42`) and keep model fallback for 12h. kicking off synthetic streaming tests against dedicated-pool-eu.

sanjay: applying temporary routing policy to direct new requests to dedicated-pool-eu and use quantized-8bit variant where acceptable: `route-policy apply --region eu --prefer dedicated-pool-eu --fallback quantized-8q`

opsbot: synthetic test results (post-mitigation): streaming p95=200ms, p99=720ms, no stalls across 1k reqs.

maria: updated #customer-impact with a short blurb: "We experienced transient increased latency and a small number of streaming retries in EU. Root cause: GPU hardware thermal events causing degraded performance on a single node. We have mitigations in place and are notifying affected customers." I'll email top-3 customers and open post-incident support thread.

incident-bot: Incident status: Monitoring (mitigated). Tag: gpu-hardware-thermal-throttle. Keep open for 1h of steady-state before closure.

james: leaving note to follow up with hardware team for RMA and postmortem owners: sanjay, katie, hardware-eng. I'll draft timeline and action items in the postmortem template. :hammer_and_wrench:
